Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Body, health & movement

pressure noun

a pressing force

also blood pressure, air pressure, water pressure, tyre pressure

classical

Vitr. 10.8 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 62: pressiō sanguinis, blood pressure
Traupman 215, 270: pressiō āeria, air pressure
M-O s.v. air pressure: āeris pressiō

pressiō, pressiōnis f.

noun, third declension

pressure, pressing

Classically a technical word of Vitruvius; Traupman and Morgan–Owens use it for blood and air pressure.

Other words

  • pressus, pressūs m. — pressure, a pressing

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 2.54: dēpellit pressum omnem ponderum

  • pressūra, pressūrae f. — pressure

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 18.317 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 280: pressūra sanguinis, blood pressure

    Lewis & Short: post-Augustan; in Pliny, one pressing of grapes or olives.

Examples

  • ut onera contentīs corporibus facilius feruntur, remissīs opprimunt, simillimē animus intentiōne suā dēpellit pressum omnem ponderum

    as loads are carried more easily when the body is braced, and crush it when it is slack, just so the mind, by bracing itself, throws off all the pressure of its burdensCic. Tusc. 2.54

See also press, force, pressure.
